payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones

program.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

requirements.text: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
requirements.source_phrase: Move the mug to the right of the headphones

outcomes.description: Move the mug so that it is positioned to the right of the headphones.
outcomes.target: The mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones.
outcomes.reference: The headphones in the image; compare the mug’s position with the headphones.

nodes.question: Does comparison of the source and edited images establish that the source mug has been relocated to the right of the headphones?
nodes.criteria: Pass when visual correspondence and spatial evidence support that the source mug has been relocated to the right of the headphones in the edited image. Evaluate correspondence using the combined evidence of body proportions, rim, handle geometry, scale, appearance, and placement; exact color or appearance preservation is not required. A mug on the right alone does not establish the requested relocation. Fail when the evidence establishes that the source mug remains left of the headphones or otherwise has not reached the requested right-side position, including identifiable movement that stops short of that position. Use unknown when competing correspondences remain unresolved and would change whether the condition is satisfied. Neither failure to prove completion nor a blurred remnant alone establishes failure.
nodes.binding: Target: the light-blue mug with a left-facing handle in the source image. Reference: the headphones in each image. Compare that mug with both edited mugs—the pale mug left of the headphones and the mug right of them—and inspect the blue blurred patch at far left as possible residual evidence. Assess the candidates without assigning identity from color alone or requiring an unchanged handle orientation. Account for the different image framing, scale, and headphone arrangement by comparing object-relative positions rather than raw pixel coordinates. Determine whether the combined evidence establishes relocation of the source mug to the right of the edited headphones; leave the result unknown if the available evidence cannot resolve that condition.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

d1: The trace overstates correspondence: the right-hand mug is on the requested side, but its dark interior, handle orientation, and overall appearance differ substantially from the source; similar taper and scale alone do not establish identity. The pale mug left of the headphones is also a candidate, and the blue blur at far left is ambiguous residual evidence—not proof either way. Tighten the decision to weigh the full set of identity cues and whether the source mug itself reached the right side, explicitly resolving competing candidates and residual evidence before passing; use unknown if that evidence remains unresolved. Do not infer failure merely from the blur or force a label from the aggregate reference. The observed yes conflicts with the partial reference, so investigate this semantic overconfidence; there is no transport, schema, or dependency failure indicated.

observations.evidence: The source light-blue mug is left of the headphones. In the edited image, the mug on the right of the headphones has a similar tapered body and rim proportions and comparable scale, supporting it as the source mug despite its different appearance and handle orientation. A separate pale mug remains left of the headphones, while the blue blurred patch at far left is consistent with residual evidence rather than the mug itself. The corresponding mug is therefore established to be right of the edited headphones.

findings.source_phrase: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
findings.question: Does the right-hand edited mug correspond to the source mug, rather than being a separate mug, with the source mug still represented elsewhere?
findings.criteria: Inspect the source mug’s distinctive shape and handle together with the edited candidates and any residual evidence. Do not infer identity from position or general mug-like appearance alone; determine whether the evidence supports relocation of the source mug to the right of the headphones.
findings.evidence: The edited image shows two small mugs: one to the left of the headphones and one to their right, plus a blue blurred patch farther left. The source mug is a larger light-blue mug with a left-facing handle. The saved observation identifies the right mug as corresponding based on similar body and rim proportions, but the edited mugs appear substantially smaller and neither visibly retains the source mug’s blue appearance; the left patch is not clearly identifiable as the source mug.
findings.rationale: The existing pass depends on resolving which edited object is the source mug. The two candidates and blurred remnant make that correspondence consequential, and the observation’s stated shape/scale evidence does not clearly settle it from the images. This is a focused identity investigation, not a claim that the requested move failed.

transactions.reason: The observed pass identifies the right-hand mug from generic taper, rim proportions and scale without resolving the competing left-hand mug. The edited candidates differ from the source in appearance and handle presentation, and the far-left blue blur is not identifiable as a mug. Revise the existing completion check to require discriminating correspondence evidence rather than treating a mug on the requested side as sufficient; retain unknown when correspondence cannot be resolved.

decisions.question: Does comparison of the source and edited images establish that the source mug itself has been moved to the right of the headphones?
decisions.criteria: Pass only when the combined visual evidence establishes both correspondence to the source mug and its position to the right of the edited headphones. Compare both edited mug candidates using body proportions, rim and interior, handle geometry, relative scale and appearance, accounting for changes in framing and possible rotation. Generic mug shape, similar taper or presence on the right is insufficient when those cues do not distinguish the right-hand candidate from the left-hand candidate. Consider evidence supporting and contradicting each correspondence; do not dismiss differences in interior, handle or appearance without weighing them together with the supporting cues. Exact color, scale and handle orientation preservation are not separate requirements. Fail when the evidence establishes that the source mug remains left of the headphones or otherwise has not reached the requested right-side position. Use unknown when the source mug's correspondence or resulting position remains unresolved. A blurred patch alone establishes neither retained identity nor successful removal, and lack of proof of completion is not proof of failure.
decisions.binding: Target: the light-blue mug with a left-facing handle in the source image. Reference: the headphones in each image. Compare the source mug with both edited candidates: the pale mug left of the headphones and the dark-interior mug right of the headphones. Inspect the far-left blue blurred patch only as ambiguous possible residual evidence, not as an identified mug. Assess whether the full cue combination distinguishes the right-hand candidate as the relocated source mug rather than a separate mug; if neither candidate can be identified reliably, return unknown. Compare object-relative placement with the edited headphones, allowing for changed framing, scale and headphone arrangement rather than relying on raw pixel coordinates.
